To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have presented efficient checkers for integer GCD and for modular exponentiation.

(a) the integer GCD problem can be checked by a deterministic polynomial time algorithm that is correct and efficient; and (b) the modular exponentiation problem can be checked in polynomial time by a deterministic algorithm that is correct, efficient, and can be implemented in a straightforward manner.

(1) efficient checkers can be constructed for the number-theoretic problems integer GCD and exponentiation modulo a composite number; and (2) these checkers are based on a new technique, which we call the “reduction technique”, that can be applied to other problems as well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing efficient checkers for programs that perform number-theoretic computations.
the design and implementation of efficient checkers for number-theoretic computations.
developing efficient checkers for programs that perform important number theoretic computations.

the program checker approach to program correctness is not only feasible, but can be efficient for certain classes of programs.
